'Unknown power' (power = '*' OR power IS NULL) can't be written with a plain WHERE (no IS NULL support) or with BUT NOT nested under a different head, so it is expressed as a correlated count-equals-zero subquery on Card, keyed by CardUuid.

answer: THE DISTINCT COUNT OF Customer [has CustomerCurrency: 'EUR'] [is of Yearmonth has YearmonthConsumption c] WHERE c > 1000
sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT custom4."CustomerID") FROM "customers" AS custom4 JOIN "yearmonth" AS yearmo5 ON yearmo5."CustomerID" = custom4."CustomerID" WHERE yearmo5."Consumption" IS NOT NULL AND yearmo5."Consumption" > ? AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 WHERE custom4."Currency" IS NOT NULL AND custom4."Currency" = ?)) AS "count"

note: The question needs, per segment (SME/LAM/KAM), the annual (2013) total consumption per customer, then the minimum of those per-customer totals (mathematically the 'average of the tied lowest' collapses to that minimum), and finally three pairwise differences of that value across the three segments in one result. That is a two-level aggregate (a MIN over a per-customer GROUPed SUM), correlated per segment, composed with cross-segment arithmetic -- a combination the primer's 20 patterns don't cover directly. I tried six phrasings: (1) a per-row correlated SUM using 'AND has ...' -- parse error; (2) 'AS t' placed after a trailing WHERE -- 'unconsumed input near AS t'; (3) correlating via 'is of Customer' in the wrong direction -- resolver error (the fact type reads Yearmonth has Customer, not the reverse); (4) correlating via a denotation on the bound CustomerID ('has Customer: !cid') -- resolved correctly but failed at SQL generation with 'node n26 has no anchor'; (5) a GROUPED BY attempt where the SUM's IN-path wasn't anchored back to the outer Customer -- an unintended cross join that ran for minutes and had to be killed; (6) correlating via a directly bound entity variable ('Customer c ... has Customer: !c'), mirroring a pattern I saw another session use successfully for a similar shape -- rejected with 'Customer is named here but joined to nothing'. Each fix addressed the previous error but exposed a new one at a different stage (parser, resolver, or SQL codegen), so I judged this genuinely not reliably expressible rather than keep guessing at compiler internals.

note: This needs, per segment (SME, LAM, KAM), the customer with the least 2013 CZK annual consumption (an argmin on THE SUM), then that same customer's annual AVERAGE consumption (a different aggregate), then pairwise arithmetic differences of those three per-segment scalars. I could get each per-segment value individually and correctly with one query each -- e.g. for SME: 'LIST c, t_sum, t_avg FROM Yearmonth ym has Customer c [has CustomerSegment: 'SME'] [has CustomerCurrency: 'CZK'] AND ALSO has YearmonthDate d1 AND ALSO has YearmonthConsumption v1 AND ALSO THE SUM OF v1 GROUPED BY c AS t_sum AND ALSO has YearmonthDate d2 AND ALSO has YearmonthConsumption v2 AND ALSO THE AVERAGE v2 GROUPED BY c AS t_avg WHERE starts_with(d1, '2013') AND starts_with(d2, '2013') ORDERED WITH t_sum ASCENDING THE FIRST 1' (gives customer 12685, average -7003.55; the same pattern gives customer 50066/average 1.12 for LAM and customer 45195/average -755.55 for KAM). But there is no construct in the primer, and none I could get to parse, for combining three independently-filtered 'argmin row' selections into one query and taking arithmetic differences between them: a (LIST ...) used as a scalar operand does not respect its own ORDERED/FIRST (silently gave a wrong, differently-ordered value), an aggregate cannot be taken over an already-GROUPED BY result ('t' IN names an attribute the path does not bind'), and FROM cannot take a parenthesised sub-SELECT as its source. So the per-segment lookups are individually expressible but the three-way combination into pairwise differences is not, as a single ConQuer-92 query against this model.
